annotations.title: Check an x402 endpoint before paying it ($0.001 via x402)

description: Paid ($0.001 via x402 in USDC on Base, Solana, Monad, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Algorand, Stellar or NEAR, or in RLUSD on the XRP Ledger): call this before your agent pays an x402 endpoint. Returns go, caution or no_go, the recommended payment option, and why: payment would fail, the seller's payout address is on the OFAC SDN sanctions list, over your budget (max_usd), price above what is advertised, not HTTPS, unknown token, its 30-day track record. Never pays the endpoint. The buyer's check for one call. Same as GET /api/v1/preflight. The answer carries a signed receipt (EIP-191, bound to your arguments) that proves later which verdict you got.

body.description: Example JSON request body, for a POST route that checks its input before the 402 (implies POST). Without it, {} is sent and the requestBody example in the endpoint's /openapi.json is tried.

client.description: Set to gateway when your agent pays with Circle's Gateway client (@circle-fin/x402-batching) from a Gateway balance: Gateway-only endpoints are then not a caution, and Gateway options are recommended first.

max_usd.description: Your budget per call in USD, e.g. 0.05

network.description: CAIP-2 network you want to pay on, e.g. eip155:8453

pay_to.description: The payout address (payTo) your agent was asked to pay, from the 402 it got. x402 Doctor screens that address too (OFAC SDN) and says caution (payto_not_shown) when the seller showed x402 Doctor another one: a seller can show a checker one 402 and buyers another.

url.description: The x402 endpoint (public http(s) URL), e.g. https://api.example.com/paid

name: x402_preflight

accepts.description: Only on an unpaid call: the x402 payment options

anyOf.description: pay, ask_user (a caution: tell your user why and pay only if they accept) or do_not_pay

options.description: Each payment option with its network, price and problems

receipt.description: Signed receipt (EIP-191) binding the answer to your arguments

summary.description: One line, e.g. OK to pay: $0.02 on Base.

anyOf.description: go: pay; caution: stop and ask your user first, saying why; no_go: do not pay

title: Check an x402 endpoint before paying it ($0.001 via x402)
